transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 16:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Anita Gomez (BrightNote Head of Search), Carlos Rivera (BrightNote Lead ML Eng), Sophie Lee (BrightNote CTO)
Shared: deck (link to slides), benchmark spreadsheet (link), sample curl snippets (link)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. We have Ethan, our SE, who will walk through embeddings and reranking today. Anita, Carlos, Sophie, thanks for making time. quick agenda, demo live, q&a, and next steps.

[00:28] Anita Gomez: Hi Maya, thanks. Quick context — BrightNote powers editorial search for our platform, currently using Elastic for retrieval and some ML-based rerank on a small set, looking to improve recall + relevance. Our main constraints are latency (<200ms on page load), cost, and data controls.

[00:50] Ethan Cho: Great, thanks Anita. I'll start with a quick overview of the hosted embeddings endpoint then jump to the reranker. We'll show how a retrieve-then-rerank pipeline looks with Redwood hosted API. I'll also show the Console where you can see per-route latency, token breakdowns, and cost estimates.

[01:12] Sophie Lee: Curious about vendor lock and whether we can run this privately later.

[01:20] Maya Patel: good call — we offer Hosted (what we'll demo), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC / on-prem). We'll cover private options in the follow-up if you want a deep-dive.

[01:45] Ethan Cho: Ok demo — I'm going to use the embeddings endpoint. Example call: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, you get back a 1536-d vector (or 768 depending on model). For the demo I'm using a curately tuned open model we've verified for semantic relevance on long docs.

[02:10] [screen share - terminal] Ethan Cho: Running a sample call now. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large","input":"How do I reset my password?"}'

[02:36] Ethan Cho: Response shows vector, latency around 28ms for this small request from our us-west region. In bulk, embeddings can be batched which increases throughput and reduces per-vector cost.

[03:05] Carlos Rivera: When you say batching, what's the memory overhead? We have 10k daily updates to the index and need to embed them nightly.

[03:20] Ethan Cho: Batching is configurable. For embeddings, you can send up to N inputs per request depending on model. Redwood Optimize will recommend batch sizes based on sequence length distribution. For nightly runs with 10k items, you'd likely run chunked batches; memory pressure is on the client side unless you use Redwood's bulk ingestion tools.

[03:45] Anita Gomez: ok and storage — do you return or log raw text? we need to ensure no PII retention on hosted.

[03:55] Maya Patel: Good point — hosted has configurable retention policies. We can set zero-data-retention for inference payloads and provide SOC2 controls. We'll share the security whitepaper.

[04:12] Ethan Cho: Next, the search flow. Typical pattern: retrieve top K candidates from your vector DB (Pinecone/Elastic/Weaviate or our optional index), then call /v1/rerank with query + K candidates to produce a re-ranked list. The reranker considers full-document context, scorer returns scores and optional explanations.

[04:48] [screen share - Console] Ethan Cho: Here's the rerank API usage — POST /v1/rerank with payload {"query":..., "candidates":[{"id":..., "text":...}, ...]}. You get back ordered candidate ids and scores. Example: we reranked 10 candidates in ~120ms for this dataset. That includes tokenizing each candidate and running a cross-encoder pass.

[05:20] Carlos Rivera: 120ms is fine for search result page loads if the retrieve step is CDN cached. What's the per-request cost implication?

[05:31] Ethan Cho: Rerank is more expensive because it scores query against full candidate text. Cost is roughly proportional to tokens processed. Our Console shows token-level cost estimate; for small candidate sets (10-20 docs) it's usually within reasonable budget. Redwood Optimize will recommend whether to rerank top 5 vs top 20 depending on your latency SLO and QPS.

[06:02] [brief crosstalk — Sophie asking about A/B tests]

[06:20] Maya Patel: We also support canary rollouts from the Console so you can A/B a reranker variant and measure click-through or kpi impact.

[06:33] Anita Gomez: Are there models you recommend out of the box? we want stable behavior across product docs and user questions.

[06:42] Ethan Cho: We have a model catalog. For embeddings we recommend rwd-embed-large for semantic search; for reranking a cross-encoder model tuned for relevance is recommended. We also provide quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads and fallback to smaller models during high load.

[07:05] Carlos Rivera: Can we bring our own model weights on Dedicated / Private?

[07:12] Maya Patel: Yes — Dedicated supports pinned model versions and Private gives you full control; you can load your own model and use Redwood's runtime for serving. We'll set up a technical deep dive if you want to explore that.

[07:35] [screen share - benchmark sheet] Ethan Cho: showing a sample benchmark spreadsheet — columns for qps, p95 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1k requests. For hosted, targets are p95 <200ms for embeddings and 100-300ms for small rerank jobs depending on candidate count.

[08:05] Anita Gomez: We need compliance info — SSO, audit logs, KMS.

[08:12] Maya Patel: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). We'll add links to our SOC2 and encryption docs in the follow-up email.

[08:32] [pause — Ethan types]

[09:00] Ethan Cho: Demoing an end-to-end pipeline — retrieve top 50 via Pinecone (client-side), call rerank with top 10 candidates. I'll show the Console trace: you can see per-request breakdowns, cache hits, and batching efficiency.

[10:10] [screen — Console trace] Ethan Cho: Notice a KV cache hit for repeated prefixes which shaves 30ms off subsequent requests in this session.

[10:40] Carlos Rivera: Interesting, what's KV cache persisted across instances?

[10:46] Ethan Cho: The KV cache is per-serving shard with TTL. For private deployments you can configure cache persistence and warm-up behavior.

[11:05] Sophie Lee: If we have EU customers, can we force region routing?

[11:11] Maya Patel: Yes — routing policies allow region pinning, and Private deployments in customer region are an option for strict residency.

[11:30] Anita Gomez: Ok, practical question — what's the instrumentation to measure relevance improvements? we track MRR and CTR.

[11:39] Ethan Cho: We provide evaluation hooks and can log reranker scores and candidate deltas. Redwood Optimize can run offline evals on a labeled prompt set and alert on regressions. You can also push custom metrics to the Console.

[12:05] [screen — sample rerank response] Ethan Cho: Sample payload shows candidate ids, original rank, new rank, and score deltas. You can choose to surface explanations in the UI or keep them internal.

[12:40] Carlos Rivera: A lot of our docs are long (4k+ tokens). How does rerank handle long docs?

[12:47] Ethan Cho: For long docs we typically chunk and embed at passage level for retrieval, then rerank either on passages or on concatenated top passages. Cross-encoder rerankers have token limits; Redwood's runtime does smart chunking and will recommend strategies via Optimize.

[13:15] Anita Gomez: If we chunk, do we lose context? sometimes the answer spans multiple passages.

[13:21] Ethan Cho: You can candidate-aggregate scores or run a second-pass context fusion. There's a tradeoff vs latency; Optimize recommends based on your labeled sets.

[13:45] Sophie Lee: Security again — do you ever store embeddings by default?

[13:50] Maya Patel: By default no, but we can configure retention. For zero retention we do not store text or embeddings; we can also enable customer-managed keys for encryption.

[14:10] Anita Gomez: What's SLAs for hosted?

[14:16] Maya Patel: Hosted has best-effort SLAs, Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. For mission-critical, customers usually pick Dedicated. We'll map expected QPS to instance sizing in the pilot.

[14:40] [Q&A dives into latency tuning — Ethan explains batching, caching, model size choices]

[16:05] Ethan Cho: Example: lowering candidate set from 20 to 5 reduces rerank latency ~2.5x and lowers token cost accordingly; but you may lose recall. That's where A/B testing is useful.

[17:00] Anita Gomez: Onboarding effort — how quickly can we get a pilot?

[17:05] Maya Patel: We can provision a trial API key and a sandbox project same day. Pilot plan: upload 500-1k sample docs and queries, run the benchmark, adjust reranker config, then run a two-week test.

[17:30] [screen — sample onboarding checklist]

[18:00] Carlos Rivera: What about data exfil prevention — if we use hosted, can we restrict who downloads logs?

[18:10] Maya Patel: Yes RBAC and audit logs; we can restrict access to logs and set retention. For full control we recommend Private.

[18:30] Sophie Lee: Any references of other editorial customers?

[18:36] Maya Patel: We have similar customers (anonymized) and a benchmark we can share — noted in the follow-up.

[19:00] [demo wrap-up — Ethan shows Console cost projections]

[20:00] Anita Gomez: Pricing model summary?

[20:05] Maya Patel: Hosted pricing is usage-based: embeddings per vector unit + rerank token units. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit. We'll send explicit numbers based on your QPS and expected token consumption.

[20:40] Carlos Rivera: If we hit spiky traffic during product launches, how do you handle bursts?

[20:49] Ethan Cho: There's burst capacity and auto-scaling policies on Redwood Dedicated. Hosted also has adaptive routing and fallback model variants but with less capacity guarantees.

[21:15] [technical tangent on model quantization and throughput]

[23:00] Ethan Cho: Also worth noting — we have a rerank-lite option that uses a lightweight cross-encoder for low-latency real-time scoring. It trades some quality for speed.

[24:30] Anita Gomez: For our pilot we'll need a reproducible eval — is there tooling?

[24:38] Ethan Cho: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses, prompt set-based regression alerts, and exportable reports. We'll attach a sample eval template.

[25:05] [customer asks about vendor comparisons: Pinecone + OpenAI embeddings]

[25:15] Maya Patel: Pinecone is a vector DB, complementary to what we do. With OpenAI you get embeddings but less visibility into production serving economics. Redwood focuses on inference serving, observability, and routing across model variants.

[26:00] Sophie Lee: Let's talk timeline — we need something in prod within Q2.

[26:06] Maya Patel: Timeline looks feasible: pilot in Apr, two-week validation, then production roll starting May if pilot goes well.

[26:25] [wrap-up recap] Maya Patel: Quick recap — we'll send pricing, SOC2/security docs, provision trial API key, Ethan will share benchmark sheets and curl examples, Carlos will provide sample queries. Next meeting we can deep-dive private deployment if needed.

[27:00] Anita Gomez: sounds good. one more thing — do you support instant feedback loop for reranker learning from clicks?

[27:10] Ethan Cho: We can log clicks and ship them to an offline retraining pipeline; Redwood can integrate with your ML workflows. Real-time online learning is possible on Private but typically done offline for stability.

[28:00] [closing pleasantries]

[28:20] Maya Patel: Thanks y'all — we'll follow up with links.

[28:30] Meeting end: 16:58 PT

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription has some mis-recognized product names (rwd-embed -> rwd-embed etc.) and occasional speaker attribution errors.
